recipes.name: Apple Butter Spice Cake
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup whole bran cereal or wheat germ

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Combine brown sugar, pecans, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a bowl. Set aside.
Sift flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt into a bowl. Set aside.

Beat white sugar and butter together in a bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy; beat in eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in apple butter, bran cereal, and vanilla extract until incorporated. Add flour mixture, alternating with sour cream, mixing well after each addition.
Pour ½ batter into the prepared baking dish; sprinkle with ½ brown sugar topping. Cover with remaining ½ batter; sprinkle with remaining ½ topping.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into center comes out clean, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Butter Spice Cake
raw_recipe.description: This apple butter spice cake recipe features apple butter, sour cream, and wholesome bran cereal, crowned with a warm-spiced, brown sugar–pecan topping.

review.reviewBody: I found this recipe when I was looking to use up a jar of apple butter a friend gave me. It is a great cake! I did some modifications; brown sugar instead of white; walnuts instead of pecans; instant oats instead of bran/wheat germ. Perfect for potluck or church socials - no messy frosting.

Oh Boy, was this good!! Easy to make too. Next time I may add 2-3 chopped apples to the cake mixture. And, will use different baking pans based on the event. Bundt, or 2 loaf pans or even muffins!!! I drizzled caramel sauce on top of cake before serving
I made this as a breakfast bread layered in a bundt pan. Only change I made was to use walnuts instead and sliced apples added to the layers. Worthy of company!

Even with a couple of heathier substitutions, it was absolutely fantastic. I used drastically less sugar, half whole wheat flour, and subbed a high protein yogurt for the sour cream. As a middle layer, I spread a thin layer of apple butter and sprinkled only a couple of tablespoons of sugar with the spices, no topping. Delish!

Utterly scrumptious! Comes out so moist, yet light-I've never seen a cake disappear so quickly! (Sadly, I'd halved the recipe, but I won't be making that mistake again.) Following others' comments, I substituted Instant Oatmeal for the bran/wheat germ. Omitted the nuts, because of our little grandchildren, and added some ground ginger to the brown sugar mixture. Thanks a mill for your wonderful recipe, Shirley-this one's a keeper!
This was a Hit, a keeper for sure. Replaced wheat germ with maple instant oatmeal. More like a coffee cake. Drizzled with caramel syrup after it cooled. Took for potluck.
I made this cake for our annual family pumpkin carving/dinner. I used my bundt pan and also added 1 1/2 c. chopped apples as other reviews suggested. I also put a sugar glaze on the cake. Very good.
Good flavor. But don't bake it 40 min in a 9x13! Probably more like 30 mins and if using a dark pan, set oven to 325.

I enjoyed this cake a lot. Very easy and quick to make. I didn't need a 13X9 cake, so I cut the recipe in half and baked it in a smaller square pan. Like others, I didn't have any bran cereal or wheat germ so I subbed in rolled oats with no discernible difference. I also cut back on the sugar a bit. A flavorful, moist cake I'll make again and again.

I made muffins out of this recipe. I used APPLE CIDER apple butter and I cut the sugar in the actual bread recipe in half. For muffins, there was a little too much topping (and imo, I think the topping needs butter, more like a streusel) but I'm not complaining. ;) I can't stop eating it. Quite moist, slightly chewy and VERY flavorful, one of the BEST quick breads I've had in a long time.

The only change I made was to sub 1/4 c. white sugar plus 1/2 c. brown sugar for the 1 c. white sugar in the cake. Reduced the amount a bit but was still plenty sweet and spicy. Took it to small group and all the ladies asked for the recipe. Baked for 35 min. and it was perfectly done and moist. Topped it with a dollop of fresh whipped cream since it was for our group dinner. Otherwise, great without. Next time I'm going to add some raisins.
No changes. Loved at parties/potlucks.

Followed to the T so I could adjust if I wanted.did use the instant oatmeal.had a 10x13 glass pan was done at 30 minutes.husband was very complimentary.if were to cut back sugar maybe 3/4 C on the brown sugar in the topping!
This tastes better as each day goes by!
Can’t tell you what it tastes like, but it smells good. Just out of the oven. Easy to make. I mixed all dry ingredients and added the liquid ingredients gradually, the eggs last and one at a time.

Having read reviews prior to making this delicious cake, I did reduce the amount of brown sugar in the topping to limit sweetness a bit. This cake is indeed moist and fluffy, I also used plain vanilla yogurt rather than sour cream as another reviewer suggested. Absolutely will share with family and friends and make this again!! Yumm Yumm!

I perked this up a little with some clove, allspice, and ginger to really round out the spice mixture, I also used freshly grated nutmeg. I took it to two houses for Thanksgiving, and everyone loved it.
I chose this recipe because it has both apple butter and sour cream which I needed to use up. I used oatmeal instead of cereal/wheat germ. Definitely a keeper.
My family can’t get enough of this cake. It’s perfect for holiday gatherings.
Excellent!
